items.headline: Contract vs spot (KB Securities, third-party est., 20 Nov): KB sees 2027 DRAM demand +25% against supply +18%, with key customers receiving only ~70% of what they need, and forecasts Samsung/SK hynix contract DRAM ASPs +40% and NAND +30% in 2027; it says DRAM and NAND spot fell ~5% and ~20% in the past month while contract prices kept rising, putting the spot–contract gap above 20%, and calls chip-stock pessimism 'near its peak'. Samsung and SK hynix were down ~4% and ~5% in Korean pre-market trading after the US chip sell-off (Edaily (KB Securities estimate); Financial News, 2026-11-20)

Lynx Equity (KC Rajkumar) named Micron its top semiconductor pick and kept a $1,325 target, calling the stock 'ridiculously cheap' at ~2.3x his calendar-2028 EPS estimate; he argues slower data-centre permitting does not mean weaker DRAM/NAND demand (Investing.com, 2026-11-19)
MU closed $690.44 on 2026-11-19, -13.5% vs $798.44 on 2026-11-12 (Nasdaq.com official closes)

MU fell 2.10% on 19 Nov to close at $690.44 (from $705.27; range $689.27–$760.00, ~35M shares), its sixth straight decline and lowest close since 6 Nov, after opening near $740 on Anthropic's Nasdaq debut and reversing as AI and chip stocks sold off (S&P 500 −2.0%, Nasdaq −2.25%, SOX −2.4%; Nvidia −3.3%; AMD −7.7% on a Hunterbrook short report on China exports); MU traded ~$678.70 after hours (Nasdaq.com, 6:39 pm ET) (Nasdaq.com / Reuters (via Investing.com), 2026-11-19)

Earnings date confirmed: Micron will hold its FQ1 FY27 earnings call on Thursday 17 Dec 2026 at 2:30 pm Mountain time (4:30 pm ET; 05:30 SGT Fri 18 Dec), replacing the third-party 16 Dec / 23 Dec estimates. The guide is revenue $60–63B and non-GAAP EPS $38.15 ± $1.00 (Micron press release (GlobeNewswire), 2026-11-19)

Anthropic debut: ANT opened at $111.50 against the $83 IPO price, reached $115 (+38.6%) and closed up 17.1% (Reuters), but the rally faded across AI hardware as investors sold chip names to fund ANT positions (MarketWatch). Dashboard arithmetic, not a company figure: Micron's ~$1.0B Class N purchase at $83 would be marked up ~17% (~$170M, unrealised) at that close (Reuters (via Investing.com); MarketWatch, 2026-11-19)

Customer LTAs: Apple is in final-stage talks with Samsung on a 4–5-year DRAM supply deal starting 1H27 (minimum volumes, market-based pricing), after reportedly signing one with SK hynix, a break from its short-contract buying; the paper contrasts Micron's stricter SCA terms (price floors/ceilings, cash deposits, take-or-pay) (The Korea Herald, 2026-11-19)

Spot pricing (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange, third-party, 19 Nov GMT+8): DRAM spot 'no demand inquiries at all'; DDR5 16Gb $60.667 (+0.28%), DDR4 16Gb $78.75 (−0.25%), DDR4 8Gb $43.921 (−0.25%). NAND: TLC 512Gb wafer spot $14.20 (−24% m/m) and 1Tb −14%; TrendForce (est.) now sees overall NAND contract prices −0–5% q/q in 1Q27 as lower Chinese CSP enterprise-SSD demand offsets North America (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange; MoneyToday, 2026-11-19)

RBC Capital (Srini Pajjuri) reiterated Outperform and a $1,500 target after an investor meeting with Micron IR (Satya Kumar): management expects tighter industry supply in 2027–28, is not worried about de-spec'ing, sounded confident SCAs are enforceable, and intends to return 100% of excess cash over time, mainly via buybacks; RBC calls the pullback an opportunity (MU ~4.2x CY27E EPS, RBC est.) (Investing.com / MarketBeat, 2026-11-18)

MU fell 1.00% on 18 Nov to close at $705.27 (from $712.42; range $687.34–$722.95, ~27M shares), its fifth straight decline, giving back a ~4.8% after-hours gain from Nvidia's results as NAND-glut worries (GF Securities) kept memory names under pressure (SanDisk −2.6% ahead of its 8-for-1 split); MU traded ~$714 after hours (Nasdaq.com, 6:38 pm ET) (Nasdaq.com / 24/7 Wall St., 2026-11-18)

Management comments: at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin, CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said demand is robust, supply tight and pricing constructive, that calendar 2027 and 2028 will be even tighter than 2026, and that 75% of Micron's 2027 output is already sold out with 2028 commitments under discussion; Micron cited 26 supply and collaboration agreements with $32B of upfront cash and financial commitments, said it still works closely with Nvidia, and reiterated that shareholder returns step up after CHIPS restrictions lapse on 9 Dec (Investing.com (event transcript) / Seeking Alpha, 2026-11-18)

DRAM/HBM pricing outlook (TrendForce Seoul roadshow, third-party est.): conventional DRAM ASPs +10–15% q/q in 4Q26, then slowing to +5–10%, +3–8%, 0–5% and 0–5% q/q through 1Q–4Q27; HBM4 seen at $3–5.5/Gb in 2027 vs ≥$2.05/Gb in 2026, with HBM4E discussed above $5/Gb (Chosun Biz / FXBus (TrendForce estimate), 2026-11-18)

Spot pricing (TrendForce weekly, third-party): DRAM buyers stay on the sidelines even as some suppliers offer lower prices; DDR4 8Gb 3200 fell 1.43% w/w to $44.25 (17 Nov) while branded DDR5 held steady; NAND sellers are cutting prices to clear inventory and the NAND spot–contract gap now exceeds 20%. 18 Nov session: DDR5 16Gb $60.50 (+0.28%), DDR4 16Gb $78.95 (−0.22%), DDR4 8Gb $44.03 (−0.50%) (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange; Newspim, 2026-11-18)

Competitors: Korean coverage of Nvidia's results notes $203B of its $390B supply commitments fall in FY28; Samsung's Q3 filing says demand keeps outrunning its output increases and it has long-term memory deals with 10 large customers (10 more in talks), while SK hynix says DRAM/HBM output through 2029 is booked and is adding HBM4 packaging/test capacity for 1H27 (etnews) (Aju News / Financial News (Korea), 2026-11-18)

China competitor: CXMT CEO Mark Cao said at its 17 Nov Q3 briefing that it has signed long-term DRAM supply agreements with several tier-one customers, while its 4F² DRAM production is still awaiting customer validation (DigiTimes, 2026-11-18)

Anthropic IPO: priced at $83 a share, above the $70–78 range (sources told CNBC; ~$1.4–1.5T valuation), with Nasdaq trading (ANT) due 19 Nov; Micron's ~$1.0B Class N purchase in the private placement is at the IPO price (CNBC, 2026-11-18)

Export policy: CNBC reports the new BIS AI-chip licence rule puts Southeast Asia's data-centre build-out (Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia) at risk; the rule targets AI processors and servers rather than memory directly (CNBC, 2026-11-18)

MU slipped 0.92% on 17 Nov to close at $712.42 (from $719.02; range $666.88–$726.98, ~30.9M shares), its fourth straight decline, after falling as much as ~7% intraday on a GF Securities NAND downgrade, the DRAM antitrust ruling and a report of an NSA network outage; the S&P 500 posted its lowest close since July. After Nvidia's results MU traded about 4.8% higher after hours (~$746.5, Nasdaq.com, 6:40 pm ET) (Nasdaq.com / CNBC, 2026-11-17)

Largest HBM customer: Nvidia FQ3 FY27 revenue was $115.8B (+103% y/y; data centre $107.6B) vs ~$109.1B expected (LSEG, est.), with a FQ4 guide of $130B ±3% (no China data-centre compute assumed) and FY28 growth raised to ~75%; supply and capacity commitments rose to $390B from $279B, mainly on multi-year memory procurement (CFO commentary). Vera Rubin NVL72 is shipping. Nvidia rose ~2–4% after hours (Nvidia / CNBC, 2026-11-17)

NAND outlook (GF Securities, third-party est.): GF cut its 2027 NAND price forecast and now sees prices flat in 1Q27 then falling in each of the next three quarters, with double-digit smartphone/PC unit declines, slower enterprise-SSD orders and supply bit growth of ~28% in 2027 and ~30% in 2028; it sees SanDisk most exposed and Micron cushioned by DRAM/HBM (TIKR (GF Securities estimate), 2026-11-17)

NAND pricing (TrendForce, third-party est.): NAND spot prices fell ~20% in two weeks as Chinese traders cut inventory and YMTC pushes commodity output; BofA (est.) puts 512Gb wafers at $14.30 (−32% q/q) and 1Tb at $24.90 (−19%) and sees phone/PC NAND contracts −5–10% q/q in 1Q27, while TrendForce still forecasts enterprise SSD contract prices +15–20% q/q in 4Q26 (TrendForce / Seoul Economic Daily (BofA estimate), 2026-11-17)

DRAM spot (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange, third-party, 17 Nov GMT+8): DDR5 16Gb 4800/5600 session avg $60.333 (flat), DDR4 16Gb 3200 $79.125 (−0.32%), DDR4 8Gb 3200 $44.25 (−0.24%); Digital Times notes DDR5 spot is down 1.9% since 3 Nov and 512Gb TLC NAND wafer spot down 15.5% to $14.267 over the same period (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange; Digital Times, 2026-11-17)

Taiwan labour: Micron and its Taoyuan union resumed talks under city-led mediation on 17 Nov but did not reach agreement, disagreeing over the proposed collective-agreement framework (peace clause, dispute limits, term); the union will put Micron's offer to a member vote and a second mediation is set for 26 Nov. Micron said it will keep talking and follow all legal procedures (Liberty Times, 2026-11-17)

Anthropic IPO: sources told CNBC the IPO is likely to price above its $70–78 range after books closed at 4 pm ET on 17 Nov, with Nasdaq trading (ANT) expected on 19 Nov; Micron is buying about $1.0B of Class N stock in the $26B private placement at the IPO price (CNBC, 2026-11-17)

Largest HBM customer: in his first statement since resigning, Jensen Huang said he would be open to returning as Nvidia CEO if the board asked; Nvidia said it does not plan to reappoint him and took no questions on it on the earnings call, where interim CEO Colette Kress called it 'business as usual' (CNBC / TechCrunch, 2026-11-17)

Competitor HBM: Samsung is reportedly developing custom HBM4E for Meta with a 2nm base die from its own foundry; Nvidia has reportedly asked Samsung, SK hynix and Micron to use TSMC 3nm for its custom HBM base dies, and Micron is said to plan outsourcing base dies starting with HBM4E (industry reports, not confirmed) (TrendForce (citing The Bell / Seoul Economic Daily), 2026-11-17)

Zacks Research cut Micron from Strong Buy to Hold (Zacks Rank #3, a quantitative estimate-revision model). MarketBeat consensus as of 19 Nov: 'Moderate Buy', 40 Buy / 5 Hold, mean target $1,435.58 (third-party) (MarketBeat, 2026-11-16)

MU fell 7.62% on 16 Nov to close at $719.02 (from $778.31; range $716.38–$739.12, ~26.5M shares), its third straight decline, as chip stocks sold off ahead of Nvidia's FQ3 results (SanDisk −8.6%, Nvidia −4.1%, S&P 500 −1.9%); new US AI-chip export rules and the DRAM antitrust ruling added pressure (Nasdaq.com / Investing.com, 2026-11-16)

Taiwan labour: after the Micron Taoyuan union said on 12 Nov it would quit talks, Taoyuan's mayor had the city labour bureau start statutory mediation, and both sides agreed to resume negotiations on the afternoon of 17 Nov over bonuses and profit sharing; no production impact reported (China Times, 2026-11-16)

Export policy: a Commerce (BIS) interim final rule now requires licences to ship advanced AI chips to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil (US-headquartered buyers exempt if they report) and to serve significant compute to China-headquartered firms from overseas data centres (90 days for existing customers). It targets AI processors, not memory directly; HBM to China was already restricted. Singapore's MDDI/METI said on 17 Nov they are studying the impact (Fortune / NBC News, 2026-11-16)

NAND pricing turn (Bank of America, third-party est.): NAND spot prices have fallen about 20% since mid-to-late October and 512Gb wafer spot is $14.30 (−12% w/w, −32% q/q) on weaker PC/smartphone and Chinese cloud orders; BofA sees general-IT NAND down another 5–10% in 1Q27 but kept DRAM forecasts of +8% in 4Q26 and +5% in 1Q27, and says AI data-centre (enterprise) demand is intact. Samsung fell 4.5%, SK hynix 7.9% and Kioxia 7.7% on 16 Nov (Seoul Economic Daily (BofA estimate), 2026-11-16)

Competitor HBM: SK hynix's Q3 report shows its largest customer (believed to be Nvidia) at ₩34.98T of 9M revenue (14.8%), with about ₩17.4T in Q3 alone; DRAM ASP rose by the high-20s % q/q on a larger HBM4 mix, and LTAs with 14 customers cover more than half of 2027–28 capacity (MoneyToday, 2026-11-16)

DRAM spot (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange, third-party, 16 Nov GMT+8): DDR5 16Gb 4800/5600 session avg $60.333 (+0.11%), DDR4 16Gb 3200 $79.375 (−0.16%), DDR4 8Gb 3200 $44.357 (−0.40%); DDRWatcher (est.) says DDR4 is in a fifth straight weekly decline while DDR5 sits 1.8% below its 42-week high, with no contract reset yet (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange, 2026-11-16)

Legal: US District Judge Noël Wise (N.D. Cal.) denied Micron, Samsung and SK hynix's joint motion to dismiss a proposed consumer class action (Garciaguirre v. Samsung) alleging coordinated conventional-DRAM supply cuts and a pivot to HBM; a pleading-stage ruling, nothing proven. Answers are due 7 Dec; first case conference 12 Jan 2027 (Tom's Hardware / TechPowerUp, 2026-11-15)

Week ahead: Nvidia, Micron's largest HBM customer, reports FQ3 after the US close on 17 Nov (about 05:20 SGT 18 Nov), its first results since Jensen Huang's exit, against its $108B guide; consensus ~$109.2B revenue (LSEG, third-party est.). Applied Materials guided 2027 wafer-fab-equipment spending up more than 30% (Daily Silicon (LSEG consensus est.), 2026-11-15)

Policy: the US and eight partners (Japan, South Korea, UK, Australia, Israel, India, Qatar, UAE) signed the Pax Silica 'San Francisco Declaration' on 15 Nov, setting a shared list of sensitive AI technologies and supply links incl. semiconductors and advanced packaging; full text and enforcement annexes not yet published; EU, Germany, Netherlands and Sweden deferred (East Asia Brief, 2026-11-15)

Largest HBM customer: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent gave Nvidia's board 10 days to answer whether shell companies were used to evade China export controls, said nothing above the H200 may be sold to China and urged an outside CEO; on 16 Nov CNBC (source) reported the board is not considering bringing back Jensen Huang (CNBC, 2026-11-15)

HBM share (Hana Securities, third-party est., 13 Nov): 2027 HBM shipments of 39.2B Gb split SK hynix 47%, Samsung 41%, Micron 12% (4.8B Gb), with Samsung seen leading on revenue; Micron's HBM wafer capacity est. 60K/month in 2026 rising to 80K in 2027; 2027 hyperscaler HBM demand ~44B Gb exceeds supply, with balance seen only in 2H28 (Daily Silicon (Hana Securities estimate), 2026-11-14)

MU fell 2.52% on 13 Nov to close at $778.31 (from $798.44; range ~$750–$796, ~27.7M shares) in a broad chip sell-off as investors digested Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia; the stock was down as much as ~5.4% intraday and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell over 5% (Google Finance / ChartExchange, 2026-11-13)

HBM pricing power: industry sources say Huang's exit could give HBM makers (SK hynix, Samsung, Micron) more leverage with Nvidia; SemiAnalysis (third-party est.) sees SK hynix charging Nvidia $3.00–3.30/Gb for 2027 HBM4 vs $3.70–4.10/Gb for AMD, Broadcom, Amazon and Google, and Morgan Stanley (est.) sees Nvidia's share of HBM demand falling to ~37% in 2027 with Google ~36% (The Korea Herald (SemiAnalysis / Morgan Stanley estimates), 2026-11-13)

Memory sell-off: Micron and SK hynix each fell around 5% intraday and SanDisk about 8% on 13 Nov as Nvidia slid more than 4%; Saxo's Charu Chanana said further trouble at Nvidia would hit SK hynix and Micron most, though demand from other AI accelerator platforms could cushion the impact. Nvidia reports Q3 on Tue 17 Nov (US time) (Invezz (Saxo commentary), 2026-11-13)

Competitor supply discipline: Samsung and SK hynix are shifting to 'secure volume first, invest in stages', building clean rooms but pacing tool move-ins; SK hynix has 5-year LTAs with 14 customers covering over 50% of 2027–28 capacity (DRAM and HBM effectively sold out through 2029 incl. talks), while Samsung has multi-year deals with 10 large customers and is negotiating with 10 more, targeting 60–70% LTA coverage by 2030 (Hanyang Economy / Korea JoongAng Daily, 2026-11-13)

DRAM spot (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange, third-party, 13 Nov GMT+8): DDR5 16Gb 4800/5600 session avg $60.267 (+0.06%), DDR4 16Gb 3200 $79.50 (−0.31%), DDR4 8Gb 3200 $44.536 (−0.40%); DDRWatcher (est.) flags DDR4 spot down a fourth straight week (−2.7% w/w) and DDR5 −1.4% w/w, with module and contract prices still firm (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange, 2026-11-13)
